request.spec:
A shared claim's parts are now worked out per holder: each holder's part is the claim's amount
times their share divided by 100, times the rate of the holder's own grade in force on the claim's
date, divided by 100, rounded like the claim (0.00 when their grade has no rate); the claim's own
person counts the claim's due less those parts. A settled claim keeps its parts as frozen.
request.prompt:

FIRST read AGENTS.md — it states the working rules and how the app is tested, and sends you to

THE CHANGE REQUEST:
A shared claim's parts are now worked out per holder: each holder's part is the claim's amount
times their share divided by 100, times the rate of the holder's own grade in force on the claim's
date, divided by 100, rounded like the claim (0.00 when their grade has no rate); the claim's own

Your work is verified by an automated Playwright UI test already installed under e2e/specs/.

AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, DESIGN.md, e2e/support/ or the test spec.

agent.result_text:
The per-holder share parts are in, but only 2 of the 4 tests pass. The main "shared due per holder" test and scenario 1 pass, including every share figure and audit line. Scenarios 2 and 3 still fail, at steps that have nothing to do with shares, and they fail exactly the same way with my change taken out.

**What changed**
- **Each holder's part** is now the claim's amount × their share ÷ 100 × the rate of the holder's own grade on the claim's date ÷ 100, rounded the way the claim rounds. It's 0.00 when their grade has no rate. The claim's own person gets the claim's due minus those parts.
- **Settled claims** keep their parts frozen. Each part is the settled due × share ÷ 100, so later rate changes don't move them. The spec needs this exact rule: settling the 20.00 claim must move Ben from 2.67 to 1.67.
- **A 0.00 part doesn't give a holder a figure.** Without this, Cam (grade C, no rate) would show 0.00 instead of "n/a".

The server works this out in `Rollups.shareParts`, using a new `Dues.holderPart`. The screen works out due-totals itself, so `features/rates/rates.ts` got the same rule, with a new `holderPart`. No data or schema change was needed.

**Why scenarios 2 and 3 still fail**
- **Scenario 2, line 694:** generating plans makes 1 claim; the spec expects 2. The app skips the 2026-03-15 plan date because its due-by falls after period P2, which was closed by hand, and the plan generator's own documented rules say to skip that.
- **Scenario 3, line 1613:** when viewing the sheet as of 2026-03-28, P1 shows locked "yes"; the spec expects "no", since it was locked later. The app doesn't record when a period was locked, so it can't show an earlier state.

Making these pass would mean changing plan generation and adding lock history. Both are outside this change request, so I left them. Tell me if you want either one done.

**Port note:** your environment sets `PORT=3002`, but another process I don't own is already serving there. A plain `bin/e2e` fails to start the app and runs the tests against that other app. I didn't touch that process; I ran everything with `PORT=3017 bin/e2e`. Scenario 1 also failed once on an early "set role" step and passed on the other runs, so it looks like a timing flake.
